name: GameSupport
author: Alastair M. Robinson

provenance.note: Released by its own author, who describes it in the upload as a previously-unreleased extension published so that his AMRWolf demo could be shared with source. Slot 23 comes from the guide and the readme, which agree. NOTE the version disagreement: the Aminet readme's Version field says 1.0 while the binary's own $VER cookie says 1.2. The cookie is taken as authoritative, as it is for LDos. THE SOURCE IS PARTIAL, and this note used to claim otherwise: GameSupport.s is the extension shell only -- the token table, the cold start, the C2P wrappers -- and it `include`s six files the archive does not carry (Labels1-9.s, MusicRoutines.s, SubRoutines/PlayRoutine.s, SubRoutines/Encode.s, SubRoutines/Decode.s, subroutines/codemods.s). Those hold the bodies of every controller, music, passcode and code-module keyword, which is most of the extension. The shell is still worth reading -- it is where the library opens are -- but the keywords need `extdis` like everything else.
provenance.redistribution: Distribution: Aminet, per the upload's own header, and released by the author himself with source. No licence text ships with it, so the terms beyond Aminet distribution are unstated.

findings: The name is a description rather than a product line: it is the handful of routines one game needed, not a general framework. Its cold start opens lowlevel.library and every controller keyword goes through it, answering error 0 "lowlevel.library not available" when it is absent, so nothing there could run before src/amiga/lowlevel.ts existed. NOTE the cold start itself does not fail when a library is missing: it stores zero and each keyword checks for itself. It also opens workbench.library, icon.library, its own GSDrivers/gsjoystick.library (GSReadCType/GSReadButtons, behind gscontrollertype and gsreadsega) and a C2P library, none of which ship in the archive. The partial source is described in provenance.note: it is NOT the free ride to faithful this field used to claim.
notes: The handful of routines one game needed — controller reading through lowlevel.library, a timer, mouse deltas and module playback.
